$ hemma help list
exit: 0
--- stdout ---
--- stderr ---
hemma list — overview: hosts, domains, services, and auth groups

Usage: hemma list [--all] [--policy] [--json]

By default the services list is filtered to those running on THIS host
(matched by local IP).

The PUBLIC column echoes the service's declared 'public' field: 'yes' means
hemma generates a tunnel ingress entry for the FQDN in this host's cloudflared
config.yml (alongside the internal horizon — Pi-hole record + Caddy block);
'no' means internal horizon only. This is a direct echo of the declaration,
not an observation of foreign state — hemma is the sole author of config.yml,
so there is nothing else to reconcile against. If defaults.tunnel-dir isn't
set, a 'public: true' service has no config.yml entry generated for it yet;
'hemma doctor' flags that drift.

When any auth group exists, a Groups section follows the services table: the
union of the auth provider's users database (user -> groups, read-only) and
services.yaml (service -> auth groups), one block per group, showing its users
and the services restricted to it. One-sided groups still list (services but
no users = nobody can access; users but no services). If the users database is
missing or unreadable, a services-only view is shown with a note. Usernames
only; never password hashes or emails.

Flags:
  -a, --all      Show services on every host, not just this one.
      --policy   Add LOCAL and PUBLIC columns: the auth.policy each horizon
                 requires (bypass, one_factor, two_factor, deny; unset =
                 one_factor). '-' when the auth mode carries no policy —
                 only 'forward' does. PUBLIC is shown even when TUNNEL is
                 'no': the policy is declared, it just never fires from the
                 internet.
      --json     Print a JSON array of {name, fqdn, host, backend, auth_mode,
                 policy_local, policy_public, tunnel} objects (every service,
                 regardless of host) for scripts; suppresses everything else.
                 The policy fields are omitted unless auth_mode is 'forward'.
